title: Canonical prompt envelope normalizer & template-stitcher to unblock profile publish for pinned models
creator: Aisha Patel
description: When pinning models and publishing their performance profiles we sometimes see failures caused by small differences between the model bundle's chat template and Redwood's canonical chat envelope. These differences (role delimiter variants, stray whitespace/newlines, and embedded control characters used by some third-party templates) cause the tokenization step in the onboarding pipeline to produce misaligned prefix lengths and occasionally false negatives for KV cache checks. This ticket implements a normalization and "stitching" step in onboarding that canonicalizes prompt envelopes and reconciles template variants so that token-alignment checks and profile publishing are robust across template quirks.
background: Several customer onboarding attempts in the last quarter were blocked by failed profile publishes. Postmortem (ENG-370900) called out that ~18% of failures stem from template delimiters and role-escape variations in model bundles (e.g., 'Assistant:' vs '\u2410assistant\u2411', narrow non-breaking spaces, or embedded control markers). Existing fixes have been ad-hoc and model-specific. We need a systematic sanitizer and a deterministic template-stitcher that runs before tokenization and before the performance-profile publisher can mark a model as publishable or pin-ready.
proposed_solution: Add a Prompt Envelope Normalizer in the onboarding pipeline that: 1) maps common role delimiter variants to Redwood canonical markers, 2) collapses multi-space/newline noise while preserving explicit message separators, 3) strips or escapes known control characters while recording them as metadata. Implement a Template-Stitcher that attempts to map fields in the model bundle's chat template to the canonical chat schema (system, user, assistant) and emits a template compatibility report with a 'token_alignment_score' and 'compatibility_flags'. The performance-profile-publisher will be gated: publish if token_alignment_score >= 0.95 OR if an explicit override label 'allow-legacy-template' is present and a manual QA flag is set. Add unit and e2e tests and telemetry to measure mismatch rate.
acceptance_criteria: Onboarding pipeline includes a Prompt Envelope Normalizer stage and produces a template compatibility report for every model bundle
New metric onboarding.tokenizer.mismatch_rate drops by >= 80% for bundles that previously failed due to delimiter variants (when normalization succeeds)
Performance profile publish is blocked when token_alignment_score < 0.95 and no manual override; otherwise publishes with audit log entry
End-to-end smoke tests in the onboarding CI simulate 6 known template variants and assert publish outcomes and metrics
Documentation in onboarding runbook and console UI includes the compatibility report and a short remediation guide
tasks: Add prompt_envelope_normalizer module to onboarding service (runtime/onboarding/normalizer)
Implement template_stitcher that maps bundle templates to canonical schema and computes token_alignment_score
Expose compatibility_flags and token_alignment_score to profile-publisher and Console UI
Add unit tests for at least 12 delimiter variants and unusual unicode separators
Add e2e onboarding CI job that runs the six real-world failing bundles from ENG-370900
Update onboarding docs + runbook with remediation steps and override process
Create migration plan for already-pinned models and re-run profile publish where appropriate
risks: Normalization could inadvertently alter user-visible prompts if not carefully tested (risk: prompt drift)
Overly permissive auto-fixes might mask upstream model bundle bugs leading to subtle quality regressions
Performance impact in onboarding: added normalization increases CPU cost and wall-clock time for large bundles
Edge cases with zero-width or rare Unicode separators may require iterative updates after initial rollout
notes: Design decision: prefer non-destructive normalizations (record changes in metadata; keep original text in object store) to allow audits and manual rollback
Compatibility threshold (0.95) chosen after running local experiments on 120 bundles — balances safety and unlock rate
Manual override flow requires a sign-off from model-onboarding-qa group and creates an audit ticket in Confluence
We should consider exposing 'normalizer preview' in Console for enterprise customers before forcing normalization in Private deployments
